text:
InfraBot: [ALERT] SRV lookup error rate >30% for service=api-gateway in us-west-2b. Alert ID INC-2026-0423. Observed increases in SERVFAIL and timeout for Consul SRV queries. Paging on-call: @Maya L.

Maya L: oncall here — seeing the page. beginning triage. @Alex W can you take infra checks in us-west-2b? I'll start customer impact assessment.

Alex W: on it. quick look: listing coredns pods in infra ns.
```
kubectl get pods -n infra -l k8s-app=coredns -o wide --context=us-west-2b
```
I see several coredns pods in CrashLoopBackOff and some nodes reporting network unreachable to 10.0.x.x.

Samir P: pulling coredns logs now, lots of connection errors to consul backend:
```
2026-04-23T11:14:02Z coredns[1]: plugin/forward: failed to forward to 10.0.8.12: dial tcp 10.0.8.12:53: connect: connection refused
2026-04-23T11:14:03Z coredns[1]: lookup _grpc._tcp.service.consul. on 127.0.0.11:53: SERVFAIL
```

Elena R: provider console shows "partial AZ peering degradation" for us-west-2b affecting east-west traffic between AZs. Link: https://cloud-status.example/incidents/peering-us-west-2b (internal link). This matches the node network unreachable messages.

Maya L: customer impact quick assessment: some Dedicated customers with clusters pinned to us-west-2b are seeing service discovery failures and increased API errors (5xx) for control-plane calls. Edge/API traffic that relies on SRV lookups for upstream routing is 5-10% error increase. Not global but multiple customers affected.

Alex W: short-term mitigations I can do now:
- patch coredns deployment to increase replicas and use hostNetwork on healthy nodes
- add forwarders to us-west-2a dns nodes (10.0.10.11, 10.0.10.12) as emergency fallback
- update smart-router policy to prefer us-west-2a for affected service tags
I'll run the replica bump and forwarder config now.

Samir P: reproduced a failing SRV lookup from a control-plane pod:
```
dig +noall +answer @10.0.8.12 _grpc._tcp.service.consul SRV
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
```
Forwarding the queries to 10.0.10.11 returns valid SRV for the same query.

Maya L: good. Alex, proceed with changes. I'll notify SRE and open a status page incident. tagging @PagerDuty to notify customers on higher tiers.

OpsBot: INC created INC-2026-0423 DNS-SRV-AZ-PEER. Priority: P1. Incident channel: #incidents.

Alex W: patch applied: coredns replicas scaled to 6, hostNetwork enabled on two nodes in us-west-2b that still have healthy peering to the router. Added fallback forwards to us-west-2a. Rolling restart triggered.
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/coredns -n infra
```

Samir P: after the forwarder change, observed SRV success rates back to ~98% from affected control-plane hosts. Latency for resolution still slightly elevated (~120ms -> ~350ms) while peering issues persist.

Elena R: reached out to provider support, case #CS-99877 opened — they're investigating eBGP/peering fabric in us-west-2b. ETA unknown.

Maya L: handoff — I'm staying on incident lead for customer comms. Handoff to Alex W for remediation + monitoring at 1845123600. Alex, please escalate if we need region failover.

Alex W: ack. will monitor and keep on-call updated. Setting temporary routing preference to us-west-2a for the affected service tag.

PagerDuty: acknowledgment recorded. Notifying subscribed customers for P1 incident.

Maya L: action items
- update status.redwood.in with incident summary and affected regions (I'm on it)
- Ops to coordinate with provider (Elena)
- Engineering (Alex/Samir) to monitor resolution and rollback fallbacks once peering stable

InfraBot: next update scheduled in 15 minutes or on major change. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Samir P: quick note — we added temporary cache TTL reductions so stale entries don't route traffic incorrectly. Will revert after stabilization.

Maya L: thanks everyone. Keeping this thread as the single comms stream. Will post customer-facing timeline when we have provider ETA. :thumbsup:
